chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
As for what remains on the gums, swallow it and gulp it down, and whatever is between the teeth, throw it out.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on food stuck in the gums versus between the teeth after eating?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a practical distinction in fiqh between food adhering to the gums (litha), which is consumed to ensure nourishment, and particles lodged between the teeth (bayna al-asnan), which are discarded to maintain oral hygiene. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity (tahara) with bodily comfort, illustrating how minor details of daily life are governed by prophetic tradition.
